newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, AA trades prevail.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, AA trades prevail.

text.p: Trading on London's whites sugar futures market concentrated on the forthcoming May expiry on Wednesday as market players exchanged physicals against paper and rolled their spot positions forward.
Volume was boosted by a hefty number of against actuals trades and the nearby May/August spread narrowed slightly to a $2.50/2.80 range after $3.00 earlier.
Some trade sales were also noted as pre-hedging activity ahead of the weekly European Union tender for sugar export licences, which was countered by light buying from brokers and other trade players.
Price movements were fairly tight. At 1115 GMT May stood 40 cents lower at $310.20 and August was unchanged at $307.70. Volume totalled 1,235 lots, mostly in May.

Traders said the London market was likely to see more more against actuals and crosses in the overall volume as part of the usual book-squaring before the spot May contract goes off the board next week.
"Open interest is still fairly high and after today is out there are four trading days," said one.
"Nobody is really showing their hand yet but it looks fairly quiet," he said, adding that a maximum of two European cargoes were likely to be delivered against May.
In physical news, Iran tendered to buy one cargo of white sugar for shipment between May 15 and June 15.
Earlier this week Iran was reported to have bought one to two cargoes of white sugar for the same shipment period but details of the price paid have yet to emerge.
Paris positions were also tightly mixed in a total volume of 774 lots.
May was down 30 cents at $310.20 and August up by the same amount at $307.90.
